ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a benzene ring fused with a five-membered imide-like ring; on the five-membered ring there are two carbonyl C=O groups, and one nitrogen atom is connected to R, namely N–R; in the upper right there is also a separate OH/hydroxide species. There are curved arrows in the figure, but the problem requires ignoring the arrows. Reasoning count: Count only bonds between non-hydrogen atoms, and count according to the unique connections in the structure. In the benzene ring there are 6 C–C bonds, including the fused edge shared with the five-membered ring; the two fused benzene ring carbons are respectively connected to the two carbonyl carbons, for a total of 2 bonds; the two carbonyl carbons are respectively connected to N, for a total of 2 bonds; the two carbonyl C=O bonds total 2 bonds; N–R is 1 bond. The OH in the upper right has only an O–H bond, involving hydrogen, so it is not counted. Total = 6 + 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 13.

raw_record.question_text:
In the transition-state structure shown in the image, calculate the total number of bonds in the structure, including single, double, and triple bonds but excluding those involving hydrogen.

Note: Disregard arrows. Consider all components present in the transition-state structure shown in the image.

method.method_draft: First describe the visible structure: a benzene ring fused to a five-member imide-like ring, with two C=O groups, an N–R bond, and a separate OH species; disregard the curved arrows. Count unique non-H atom-to-non-H atom bonds directly: 6 C–C bonds in the benzene ring including the fused edge, 2 bonds from the fused benzene carbons to the two carbonyl carbons, 2 bonds from the carbonyl carbons to N, 2 carbonyl C=O bonds, and 1 N–R bond. The OH contributes no counted bond because its only bond is to H. Sum these categories to get 13.
